title: Choose NaviVibe’s world
question: Every card keeps Apple Music’s structure (tabs, lists, mini player, controls). The world changes type, colour, density and one signature move. Pick one, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Pressed on Shellac
options.lineage: HMV and Columbia India 78rpm record labels, the gramophone era of Tamil film music
options.thesis: Every album is pressed: the song you hear spins as a record, its label carrying the name in gold.
options.viewport: Home: large title, Top Picks as covers with their records half out of the sleeve, Recently Played shelf, and a mini player whose cover is a spinning record label.
options.risk: A spinning record is a known music-app trope; it must stay a working progress dial, never ornament.

raised.raise: No grey cards anywhere: regions separate by space and one hairline, never by a filled grey box.
One monumental element per screen (the title, the minutes, the record), everything else stays small.
Vast black; only the record that is playing carries full colour.
Downloaded and favourited songs get a stamped mark on the cover, not a badge row.
Rank by weight and case before size: fewer type sizes, harder contrast.

options.label: Cassette Inlay
options.lineage: AVM, Echo and Pyramid Tamil film cassettes and their J-card inlays
options.thesis: Every album is a cassette inlay: a coloured spine, a typed track list, Side A and Side B.
options.viewport: Home: large title, each Top Pick framed by its own colour spine with the title set vertically, track counts typed like an inlay.
options.risk: Can read as a nostalgia skin; vertical type must never carry anything you need to read quickly.

options.label: Departures Board
options.thesis: What plays next reads like a departures board: when the song changes, the letters flip.
options.viewport: Home leads with an Up Next board: next three songs as flap rows with their times; the rest of Home is standard shelves.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: the queue maps to departures and the flip is a real state change; loses on identification, travel is not music.
options.risk: The flip turns gimmicky if it runs on anything but a real song change.

options.label: Catalogue Sleeve
options.lineage: Factory Records sleeves and catalogue numbers
options.thesis: Matte black sleeves, a coded colour strip per album, catalogue numbers instead of chrome.
options.viewport: Album grid as black sleeves with colour strips.
options.case: Fuses poorly: colour codes replacing names hurt clarity, and its signature waveform plot would be invented data.
options.risk: Unreadable when codes stand in for words.
options.kept: Vast black where only the playing record carries colour.

options.label: Graphite Console
options.case: Fuses poorly: it is the grey app you rejected, in a tool’s costume.
options.kept: Separate regions by space and hairlines, never by grey boxes.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Monumental grid-built letterforms as the page.
options.viewport: Huge grid numerals for minutes listened.
options.case: Fuses poorly: listeners don’t identify with type specimens; a visible grid adds noise to lists.

options.label: Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: Songs as coupons that tear off as they play.
options.case: Fuses poorly: red and navy fight the green brand; tearing songs off is a metaphor without a job.
options.kept: States stamp onto the item instead of adding badge rows.

options.label: Timetable Rack
options.thesis: One type size; rank by weight, case and rule.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the rake and translucent glass break your no-transparency rule and phone legibility.
options.kept: Rank by weight and case before size.

canonCard.label: Apple Music, played straight
canonCard.thesis: iOS 26 Apple Music on Android at full craft, in green.
canonCard.viewport: Exactly what Apple ships: large titles, Top Picks, shelves, capsule tab bar.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Apple Music by design; this is close to what you called bland.
